title: Symmetric-algebra dehomogenization at a distinguished summand
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, B an R-algebra, e : Sym_R(R × M) ≃_R B, and G a graded R-algebra structure on B with G_n = range(e ∘ ι)^n [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Put t=e(ι(1,0)). There is a ring equivalence a : Sym_R M ≃ B_(t),0 [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] sending ι(m) to e(ι(0,m))/t and fixing R. No freeness, nontriviality or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 01OA, 01OB, 01OE and 01NG; projective bundles and their standard affine charts

proof.text: The degree-one fractions x(m)/t form an R-linear map. Extend this by the universal property to alpha : Sym_R M → B_(t),0. Evaluation ι(r,m) ↦ r+ι(m) sends t to one, so it extends to a ring map from the full localization, and restricts to beta from degree zero.

source.place: Tags 01OA, 01OB, 01OE and 01NG; projective bundles and their standard affine charts

proof.text: Symmetric algebra induction proves beta alpha fixes every element. Power-of-submodule induction on G_n proves alpha(eval(f)) has value f/t^n for f homogeneous of degree n. Every degree-zero fraction has this form, so alpha beta is the identity. Package the inverse ring homomorphisms as a ring equivalence, retaining both displayed formulas.

lean.statement: theorem exists_dehomogenization : ∃ a : SymmetricAlgebra R M ≃+* HomogeneousLocalization.Away G t, (∀ m : M, (a (ι R M m)).val = algebraMap B (Localization.Away t) (e (ι R (R × M) (0, m))) * IsLocalization.Away.invSelf t) ∧ (∀ r : R, a (algebraMap R (SymmetricAlgebra R M) r) = algebraMap R (HomogeneousLocalization.Away G t) r)
